answer: Cross-epoch drift scoring. Each identity accumulates a behavioural fingerprint per epoch: call cadence, counterparty mix, task latency. At each boundary, the agent's new fingerprint must stay within a bounded divergence (a nebula of past behaviour) or the identity is throttled. A sudden pivot to a new role lands on a costly ledge: the operator must sustain the old profile via real work for several epochs, then shift slowly, paying genuine compute and forfeiting fast role-switching. Honest agents, held on a steady trellis of consistent activity, cross epochs unpenalized.
